quests.title: The Dark Harvest
quests.offerDialogue: The dark crystals anchor the citadel's foundations — without them, four centuries of deferred maintenance arrive all at once. Three have broken loose and crept off around the grounds. Crystals shouldn't creep. Retrieve them before the east wing notices it's unsupported.
quests.activeDialogue: Three dark crystals, loose somewhere on the grounds. They glow. They hum. Occasionally they sulk.
quests.completeDialogue: All three, returned and re-anchored. The citadel stands another century. The master would thank you, were he here, which he is not, which is the usual arrangement. Take this from the treasury — the dust won't miss it.

collectible.name: Dreadspire Shard
collectible.desc: A sliver of dark crystal from the citadel's foundations. It hums when it thinks no one is listening.

quests.title: The Deep Anchors
quests.offerDialogue: The surface crystals were the easy ones. Three more have rolled INTO the citadel — the crypt, the summoning chamber, the deep ossuary. Indoor crystals are bolder. They've learned doors.
quests.activeDialogue: Three more anchors, this time within the walls. Mind the stairs; the deep ones are unlit.
quests.completeDialogue: Re-seated, all three. The foundations purr. You begin to understand why I never leave — somebody has to chase the masonry.

quests.title: The Wandering Foundations
quests.offerDialogue: Last batch — I hope. The east tower top, the poison lab, the dungeon cells. The crystals are climbing now. I do not like that they are climbing.
quests.activeDialogue: Three final anchors, scattered high and low. Bring them home before they learn to fly.
quests.completeDialogue: Whole again, root to roof. You have done more for this citadel in a day than its master in four hundred years. The dust is, I think, fond of you.

collectible.name: Citadel Keystone
collectible.desc: A re-anchored foundation crystal, gifted in gratitude. The whole citadel leans on stones like this.

quests.title: The Garrison's Effects
quests.offerDialogue: When the garrison falls each night, it re-forms by dawn — but lately the men wake without their effects. A coin, a seal, a key, all scattered across the wards. A soldier without his kit is just a sad cold draught. Gather them.
quests.activeDialogue: Three of the garrison's lost effects, somewhere in the wards. They are not proud. They will be where they fell.
quests.completeDialogue: The men will sleep easier — well, lie easier. Soldiers should die with their boots on, not hunt for them by moonlight. You have my thanks, such as a dead man's thanks are worth.

quests.title: Three Measures for the Circle
quests.offerDialogue: The circle is hungry and I am out of everything. One measure of bone dust from the vault, one phial of shadow-oil from the study, one black candle's wax from the sanctum. Bring all three before dusk or the circle pouts, and a pouting circle is no use to anyone.
quests.activeDialogue: Bone dust, shadow-oil, candle-wax. The vault, the study, the sanctum. The circle waits, hungrily.
quests.completeDialogue: Yesss. The circle is fed and the chamber stops sulking. Tell no one the recipe — least of all Vesska, who would only improve it, which is unforgivable.

quests.title: The Bone Tally
quests.offerDialogue: A thief came through the vault and my tally is short — three femurs and a favourite skull, gone into the deep ossuary where I no longer venture. Follow the gaps in the niches; one missing bone always points to the next. Bring my tally whole.
quests.activeDialogue: Three femurs and a skull, lost deeper into the ossuary. Each empty niche points the way to the next.
quests.completeDialogue: Every bone home, every niche filled. Order restored. The skull I shall set back in its listening-spot — it has missed our little chats, I think.

quests.title: Candles for the Dark
quests.offerDialogue: The shadow will not be prayed to by honest flame. I need three black candles — two left in the shrine, one carried off into the sanctum. Gather them and the dark will hold its evening audience.
quests.activeDialogue: Three black candles for the shadow's audience. The shrine, and the sanctum beyond.
quests.completeDialogue: The dark accepts its candles. It says nothing, as is its way, but the silence is a little warmer now. Go in shadow, pilgrim.

quests.title: The Ravens' Domain
quests.offerDialogue: My birds fly the whole citadel and drop their little tokens in its furthest corners — the east tower, the cells, the war room, the poison lab. Bring me one from each corner and I will know my domain is whole, and my count correct.
quests.activeDialogue: Four raven tokens, one from each far corner of the citadel.
quests.completeDialogue: Four corners, four tokens, one whole domain. The birds settle. They like you — or they have decided not to remember you unkindly, which from a raven is the same as love.

quests.title: The Sixth Raven
quests.offerDialogue: Five ravens I count, and five return. The sixth has not. I found one black feather caught in the gatehouse — start there. A raven that drops a feather is a raven that is frightened, and mine do not frighten easily.
quests.activeDialogue: One lost feather in the gatehouse guardroom — the trail to my sixth raven.
quests.completeDialogue: The feather is hers, no doubt of it. She is sulking in the rafters, not stolen. Six ravens, six returned. You have my count and my thanks.

quests.title: The Master's Old Keys
quests.offerDialogue: Four centuries of sweeping and I have dropped the master's old keys on my rounds — undercroft, crypt, war room, in that order, I think. One key always lies near the dust of the next. Bring them back before I have to dust them, too.
quests.activeDialogue: Three old keys, dropped along Isolde's eternal rounds. Each lies near the trail to the next.
quests.completeDialogue: All three, back on their ring. Now I can lock doors I will only sweep through anyway. Thank you, warm one. It is good to finish a chore for once.

quests.title: Moon-Herbs from the Marsh
quests.offerDialogue: My poisons are dull because my herbs are dead. The only proper moon-herbs grow in Hollowmere's marsh, under that hedge-witch Morwen's watchful eye. Take her my request, gather two good bunches from the marsh, and bring them back to me. Mind her temper; it is worse than mine, and that is saying something.
quests.activeDialogue: Carry my request to Hedge-Witch Morwen in Hollowmere, then gather two bunches of moon-herbs from the marsh.
quests.completeDialogue: Fresh moon-herbs, still cold with marsh-dew. NOW we have poison with conviction. Morwen didn't curse you, I hope? She usually saves the good curses for me.

collectible.name: Moon-Herb Vial
collectible.desc: A vial of marsh-cold moon-herb distillate. Medicine with conviction, as Sythe would say.

quests.title: A Question of Taste
quests.offerDialogue: With the moon-herbs working I can finally test the base. I need two test-fungi — one from my own lab shelf, one that grows wild in the deep ossuary. Do not taste them. I mean it. The LAST assistant tasted them.
quests.activeDialogue: Two test-fungi: one in the poison lab, one in the deep ossuary. Do not taste them.
quests.completeDialogue: Both fungi, untouched, undigested — excellent. You may yet outlive my other assistants, who number, at last count, none.

quests.title: Spent Sigil-Stones
quests.offerDialogue: Sigils burn out, like everything. Three spent sigil-stones lie about the towers and the chamber — the study, the west tower, the summoning chamber. Gather them before someone steps on one and learns what a spent sigil does on its way out.
quests.activeDialogue: Three cracked sigil-stones: the study, the west tower, the summoning chamber.
quests.completeDialogue: Spent, every one, and safely in my jar. A cracked sigil is a small disaster waiting for a bare foot. You have prevented at least three minor catastrophes. Most people manage none.

quests.title: Coins for the Tombs
quests.offerDialogue: The garrison's graves go without their coins, and the dead grow restless when unpaid. Three grave-coins lie loose among the tombs of the outer ward. Gather them, and we shall lay them properly so the dead may rest and stop their nightly re-forming.
quests.activeDialogue: Three grave-coins, loose among the tombs of the outer ward.
quests.completeDialogue: Paid in full, the lot of them. The dead are quieter already — they re-form from habit now, not grievance. A small mercy, but mercy is rare currency here.

quests.title: What the Ritual Does
quests.offerDialogue: A confidence, warm one. The master's homecoming ritual does not bring him home — it brings something WEARING him. I have proof scattered as loose pages: one in this study, one in the war room, one beneath the very throne. Bring them to me, quietly. Ordrin must not know I doubt the circle.
quests.activeDialogue: Three pages of evidence: the study, the war room, beneath the throne. Quietly, now.
quests.completeDialogue: All three pages. Read together they are damning. The ritual is a door, and what knocks on the far side is not our master. I will need leave from the warden to reach the one prisoner who saw it done. Help me get it.

quests.title: Leave from the Warden
quests.offerDialogue: Take my writ to Warden Gholl. He outranks dust — barely — and the sealed lower vault answers to his key. Tell him the pages say what I dared not. He will know my hand, and the door will open.
quests.activeDialogue: Carry Vesska's writ down to Warden Gholl in the dungeon cells. His leave unseals the lower vault.
quests.completeDialogue: Vesska's hand, right enough. And the pages... gods. The vault is yours, warm one — what's left in it deserves the air. Mind the prisoner. Four hundred years alone does things to a voice.

quests.title: The Defector's Testimony
quests.offerDialogue: Air. Real air. Listen — I SAW the ritual done, and I will swear to it, but my word means nothing from inside a vault. Carry my testimony to Vesska. If anyone can stop the master's homecoming, it is that infuriating, brilliant warlock. Go. Quickly, while I still believe in tomorrow.
quests.activeDialogue: Carry Sera's testimony up to Warlock Vesska in the keep study.
quests.completeDialogue: Sera's testimony, in her own shaking hand. It is enough. The ritual will not be completed — not while I draw breath, and I intend to draw it spitefully and for a very long time. You have saved this citadel from its own master. Take this, with my regard, which I do not give lightly.

collectible.name: The Sealed Writ
collectible.desc: Vesska's order halting the master's homecoming ritual. The citadel keeps its empty throne — and is glad of it.

quests.title: The Final Record
quests.offerDialogue: In four centuries of service, few have earned what you have from me, traveller: trust. There is a record I keep for no one but myself. Sit a while. Let an old dead administrator show you.
quests.activeDialogue: Take your time. The citadel has kept its secrets far longer than either of us has drawn breath — or not, in my case.
quests.completeDialogue: There. Not every visitor earns a place in Dreadspire's true ledger. You have. The citadel will remember you long after it has forgotten most of the living.

quests.title: Out of the Dungeon
quests.offerDialogue: You. I don't like the look of you skulking near my cells. Fine — prove you're not another prisoner in waiting and report back once you've done something useful.
quests.activeDialogue: Well? The cells don't watch themselves.
quests.completeDialogue: Hmph. Took you long enough. Take it and stay clear of my dungeon from here on.

greet.text: Warm one. You move through my citadel like you belong here. I have not decided whether that pleases me.

ally.text: Then we are allies, and I shall pretend that is not a relief. Few here have a pulse, fewer still a spine.

rival.text: Defiant. Good. A circle needs resistance or it grows lazy. Cross me carefully, then.

lore.text: A door dressed as a homecoming. The master walks in; something else walks out. I would very much like to keep that door shut.

greet.text: Grave moss, is it? From the fog out past the walls. Bring me two handfuls and I'll brew you something with a bit more bite than tea.

choices.label: Brew a wraith tonic (2 grave moss)

effects.missingText: Two handfuls, I said. The fog only sits thick over Gravemoor — dig there while it clings low.
effects.successText: She swirls the moss into a simmering flask until it turns the colour of old bruises. One wraith tonic, still warm. Don't drink it yourself.

the-castellan.1: Ah, the warm one returns. The dust spoke well of you. The dust speaks of little else, frankly.
the-castellan.2: You are becoming a fixture, like the braziers, but warmer and less prone to wandering.
the-castellan.3: Four hundred years I have kept this citadel alone. It is... less lonely, lately. Do not tell the dust I said so.

raven-keeper-corvane.1: The birds have stopped warning me when you approach. From a raven, that is a knighthood.
raven-keeper-corvane.2: Six ravens, and all six watch you kindly now. I have never known them to agree on anything.

ally.1: For a friend of the tally, the deep niches are open. Mind the draught — and the things that enjoy it.

rival.1: You count bones like a thief counts exits. I am watching you, warm one. Every femur.
You've been spending time with Vesska, haven't you? I can smell the shadow-oil on you. MY shadow-oil, probably. The circle noticed. The circle is not pleased.
